record.excerpt: So I took the pure long-side Turtle code — 20-day breakout, 10-day exit, ATR stops — and let it loose on: … Including: Bitcoin & Ethereum … Buy when price breaks above the highest high of the last 20 days. … Exit when price reverses direction for 10 days. … 18 years of data (2007-2025) … Total profit across all 43 markets: $1,147,318 … It's completely misleading.
record.notes: Turtle 20/10 Donchian long-only; result is pooled over 43 futures markets incl. BTC/ETH, so per-asset claim is not stated; author himself calls aggregate misleading.

issues.problem: Claimant names Bitcoin and Ethereum as included markets, spec leaves assets empty so nothing is tested
Claimant defines entry as break above highest high of the last 20 days, spec leaves entry empty
Claimant defines exit as 10-day reversal/exit, spec leaves exit empty
Claimant includes ATR stops as part of the rule, spec encodes no ATR stop multiplier
Spec marks claim untestable due to portfolio aggregate, but the 20-day breakout 10-day exit long rule on named assets is testable per-asset

Claim reports total profit across 43 markets including Bitcoin & Ethereum. Spec encodes only BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT and tests each separately, so portfolio-level $1,147,318 result cannot be reproduced. NOT EXPRESSIBLE note does not cure omission because it changes what is tested.

Claim: 'Buy when price breaks above the highest high of the last 20 days' means prior 20-day high. Spec uses highest_high(20) with offset 0 including current bar, so close > highest high including current high can never be true. Requires prior-bar offset.

Claim: 10-day exit / 'reverses direction for 10 days' interpreted as Turtle 10-day low means prior 10-day low. Spec uses lowest_low(10) with offset 0 including current bar, so close < lowest low including current low can never be true. Requires prior-bar offset.
